completeness.answered_means: a reply came back and was written into the out-file, counted by DISTINCT id. A parse refusal is an ANSWERED row whose reply the parser refused — the two counts are NOT disjoint, and up to ten answered rows may be refusals without the bar moving. A gate that treated a refusal as unanswered would report RED at 1022 / 1032 on a run this bar accepts ([[measure_on_the_rows_the_gate_scores]])
completeness.refusals_are_counted_by_cause: never dropped and never summed into a single «other». An unreadable reply is a disagreement with a name, and unreadable replies pile up wherever the answer is the quiet one ([[the_empty_class_eats_the_parse_failures]])
completeness.rule: answered 1032 / 1032 · every row's `rendering_sha256` equals its pack item's · parse refusals ≤ 10 (1%). All three, or RED
completeness.sha_rule: the pod re-renders every item from its own fields and REFUSES the whole leg if one sha does not match, so a mismatch on the Mac means the out-file and the pack have parted after the run — a copy-back error or a rebuilt pack. Either is RED
completeness.why_this_and_not_quality: the out-file is the INPUT of pass 2. What pass 2 needs from this run is that every comment has an answer and that each answer belongs to the request it was asked under. Whether the answers are GOOD is measured against docs/REFERENCE-signals-w1.md by `pass2-signals`, and by nothing here

D2 hands leg_table a view carrying these readings under the name it reads, and the proof that it is the same instrument is that the dev-200 subset reproduces r2's 136/200 and 38/49 — checked at $0 in tests/test_gate_pass1_window.py, on r2's own 200 replies

rows.formula: r2's pod was deleted 82.9 s after its last row landed, and that span carried the whole of what this line buys. r2 REGISTERED 464 rows to copy back and MEASURED 400, because its shot never fired — the scaling below divides by the MEASURED count, which is the smaller denominator and therefore the more expensive per row. rows.formula: the contract buys the margin «for the window's larger entity blocks». Measured on the two packs: mean entities per request 0.96 → 1.8023, and the rendered request they sit in 4672.4 → 4725.8 chars, a ratio of 1.011408. The margin must be ≥ that ratio, and it is 1.24× it. A rate is a property of the sample it was measured on, so the growth from that sample to this population is measured and not assumed
rows.name: REASON — the ×1.25 margin exceeds the growth it is named for

rows.formula: rung 2's ceiling is a create-elapsed and the meter stops at `pod delete`. r1 measured the span between them at {'7spsy61lpjumrz': 78.5, 'juupgp6y77jvuz': 0.1} and the worse is charged, so a real rung-2 death bills 578.5 s and not 500. That plus the full worst case must still fit the hard stop — it does, by 4.96 s, which is the honest margin
rows.name: REASON — the recovery clause is reachable WITH the measured deletion tail

rows.formula: rung 4 prices the remainder at the LARGER of the leg's mean and its LAST call, so one slow reply is priced as if every remaining call were that slow. Solved backwards at the tightest point of the run the edge is 4.833 s/call, and the slowest single call this stack has measured is 4.066 s — a factor of 1.189. The check is the DIRECTION: the edge must sit above the worst call, or a healthy pod dies on its first bad reply
rows.name: REASON — rung 4's single-call knife edge is above the slowest call measured

rows.formula: the pre-generation lines and the overhead line are disjoint by construction: ssh ends when the endpoint answers, staging and launch end when the runner starts, the load ends at the first reply, and the overhead begins at the LAST reply. The sum of the named spans equals total_seconds with generation between them
rows.name: REASON — nothing is counted twice in the seconds line

rows.formula: the bar demands answered == 1032 AND refusals ≤ 10. They are satisfiable together only because a refusal is an ANSWERED row whose reply the parser refused. Counting a refusal as unanswered would make the highest reachable answered count 1022, below the bar's own minimum, and the bar would be unmeetable by construction ([[an_expectation_no_reading_reaches]])
rows.name: REASON — the bar's two numbers are jointly reachable

h6.rule: every number docs/PROMPT-pass1-window.md prints, re-derived from the formula the contract names for it. `equals` allows 1 % — a rounding is not a finding; `below` and `at_least` check the DIRECTION. The rows that matter are the INPUT rows: the arithmetic of a money block is the same multiplication done twice and cannot disagree with itself, so what H6 catches is a population that moved, a rate whose sample is not what it claims, or an allowance carried across a re-registration without its reason

dropped_from_r2.scorer_pass1_fewshot: r2's D2 judge scored the dev gate and the fourteen against a bar. This contract has neither — its D2 readings are report-only and go through src/market_pulse/scorer.py, which is pinned above as `scorer`. A pin naming a script this run never calls is a pin nobody checks

gate.rule: a SIBLING of scripts/gate_pass1_fewshot.py. It IMPORTS every rung computation that is pure — rungs 1, 2, 3, 4 and their clock — and re-declares the ones bound to r2's own module state (the record it writes, the launch stamp it reads, the leg it takes the first reply from) plus rung 7, which is a completeness bar here and a dev gate there. r2's gate is pinned by its own sealed record and is NEVER edited

kill_clock.read: money.arithmetic.ssh_rule — the spread this ceiling is, and its four readings
kill_clock.rule: ssh dead-man ≤ 500 s of this pod's create-elapsed or KILL. r2's ceiling, unmoved: its own pod answered at ≤ 50 s, which is an upper bound INSIDE the registered spread and not a reason to lower a ceiling that two pods of 2026-08-20 never reached. One dead pod under it costs $0.1111

kill_clock.backstop_rule: and a create-anchored BACKSTOP beside it: first reply ≤ 1100 s of create-elapsed or KILL — ssh 500 + stage/launch 150 + load 450. It is what bounds the launch anchor: a stamp taken late cannot buy a window the registration never priced, and the backstop fires with no human in the path
kill_clock.one_leg_note: r2 read this rung off the FIRST registered leg because the shipped `run()` is called once per leg and re-zeros its own clock, so a minimum across legs would have returned the second leg's ~8 s and reported GO on any load whatever (Dv620). This contract has one leg, so there is no minimum to take — and the gate still reads the leg the record NAMES rather than scanning the run directory, because the defect was the scan and not the count
kill_clock.read: the `launched_at` stamp the runbook writes into the pod's run directory the moment the runner starts, copied back by --watch and recorded in results/pass1_window_run.json. It is never typed
kill_clock.rule: launch → first reply ≤ 450 s of the runner's OWN `launched_at` or KILL. A run record without `launched_at` cannot report GO on this rung — a deadline that cannot be demonstrated has not been passed (Dv605)

kill_clock.before: the run is allowed to continue past a call
kill_clock.rule: projection gate every 20 calls: the projected attempt total at MEASURED rates, with the leg's remaining calls priced and the registered overhead added, must fit the cap at the LIVE price AND the cumulative hard stop, else KILL. The registered interval is a FLOOR — the computation is local and free and --watch runs it on every poll (Dv613: an overhead a gate carries from a previous registration prices this run with a repealed number)

kill_clock.read: held by scripts/gate_pass1_window.py --watch, a BLOCKING loop
kill_clock.rule: liveness: 600 s with no new answered row and no new pod-log line → KILL. The deadline is measured from the LAST EVENT and never from create, and an event is a RISE — a failed copy that shortens a local file is not work and does not refresh it. lora-b lost 9 720 s and an arm because every rung there watched the training log and none watched a pod that had stopped working

kill_clock.read: the `--terminate-after` stamp, read back and refused on overshoot
kill_clock.rule: cumulative hard stop 6500 s, PLATFORM-held. Each pod's --terminate-after is its own create plus what the stop has left, and the overshoot it forgives is the registered 60 s

kill_clock.before: the out-file is handed to pass 2
kill_clock.on_red: RED does not delete anything already bought and does not re-run the pod: the out-file, its refusals by cause and its sha mismatches go back to the team lead with the census. A partial out-file is still the evidence, and the resume can re-ask only what has no reply — but a second pod is the recovery clause's, and the recovery clause allows one
kill_clock.read: bars.completeness — all three numbers, on the Mac after scp
kill_clock.rule: answered 1032 / 1032 · every row's `rendering_sha256` equals its pack item's · parse refusals ≤ 10 (1%). All three, or RED

arithmetic.boot_rule: ≥ the worst boot this stack has measured (353.0 s, lora-b) — r2's derivation, unmoved, and anchored on the runner's own `launched_at`. r2 added a new FLOOR on 2026-08-21 (142.709 s) and not a new ceiling: this stack's boot is not a constant and the ceiling is charged at the maximum

cumulative.backstop_tolerance_rule: how far the `--terminate-after` stamp actually handed to `pod create` may sit BEYOND the one the hard stop computes. Only overshoot is bounded — a window rounded DOWN shortens itself and is always safe. The gate READS it from here and a record without this field is a refusal, not a default
cumulative.hard_stop_rule: cumulative billed ≤ 6500 s = $1.4444 at the $0.8/h ceiling. It sits UNDER the $1.50 cap it defends and it is the PLATFORM that enforces it, so it protects even a hung call no gate can see. r2's 6 100 s does not carry over: this population is 1 032 calls and not 464, and a stop copied for its algorithm would have brought its number with it

projection_gate.formula: billed_by_closed_pods + elapsed_on_this_pod + the leg's remaining calls × its s/call + overhead_seconds. The leg is priced at its MEASURED rate — the larger of its mean and its last call — as soon as it has a reply, and at the registered rate before that
projection_gate.overhead_rule: the SAME 1 300 s the money block charges, and it has to be: rung 4 prices the attempt with it on every poll, so a second copy here is a second budget. H6 asserts the two are one number

single_call_sensitivity.what_fires_it: ONE reply slower than 4.833 s landing as the most recent row at an early poll. The slowest single call this stack has measured is 4.066 s, so the edge sits 1.19× above it — margin, not comfort. The SECONDS bind here and not the dollars: the same projection at the live price is well inside the cap
single_call_sensitivity.what_it_costs_if_it_fires: the boot and whatever was billed — not the leg. Every reply is flushed as it lands and the shipped resume skips every unit already answered, so a re-creation re-asks only what has no reply. The ONE re-creation the recovery clause buys is what pays for it, and after it there is no second
single_call_sensitivity.why_it_is_not_loosened: `leg_state` and `projection` are scripts/gate_pass1_fewshot.py's, pinned by r2's sealed record and imported here unedited. Pricing the remainder at the mean alone would be a weaker gate in the PERMISSIVE direction, which is the one these rungs exist to close. So the sensitivity is REGISTERED rather than repaired

projection_gate.verdict: KILL if the projection exceeds $1.50 at the LIVE price, or exceeds the 6500 s hard stop in seconds. The stricter binds
projection_gate.why_one_leg: r2 priced every leg still owed because its shot's 64 calls were what made the dev legs affordable. This contract has ONE leg, so «every leg still owed» and «the running leg» are the same set — the formula did not need weakening and was not weakened

cumulative.rule: the hard stop and EVERY budget check count across ALL pods of this attempt, never per pod. `--terminate-after` on each pod is stamped at that pod's create plus the hard stop LESS what every closed pod already billed, so two pods cannot each be given a fresh window
cumulative.session_ceiling_rule: cap / price ceiling — the longest session the cap can pay for. It is ≥ the hard stop, so the platform-held stop is the binding one and the cap is never what discovers an overrun

overhead_measured_on_r2.rule: the number this line did NOT move on when the rows it covers went 400 measured → 1032, and the reason it did not have to. r2's pod was deleted 82.9 s after its last row landed, and that span carried the whole of what this line buys — the final copy, the gate on the Mac and the delete. Scaled by rows it is 213.9 s against 1300 charged, a 6.08× headroom, and the scaling is generous: r2's gate ran the SCORER over its 400 rows and this contract's rung 7 only parses them. The per-poll copies are not in this span at all — they happen while the pod is generating and cost it nothing
overhead_measured_on_r2.what_that_stamp_is: the create-elapsed of the poll on which --watch SAW every row answered, not the instant the last row landed. The loop polls at 20 s, so the true last row is somewhere in (at_go − 20, at_go] and this reading is the LATER end — which makes the span below a lower bound on the overhead measured, and therefore the conservative direction ([[a_paced_log_is_an_interleavable_clock]])
overhead_measured_on_r2.why_the_two_differ: r2 budgeted the copy-back of 464 rows — 400 dev and the shot's 64 — and its shot never fired, so what its overhead line actually carried was the 400 answered. The scaling below divides by what was MEASURED, which is the smaller denominator and the more expensive per row ([[a_count_in_prose_is_not_the_enumeration]])

arithmetic.overhead_rule: 1300 s — the copy-back of ≤ 1032 rows on every poll, the completeness gate on the Mac, and the deletion with its three listings. ssh and staging have their own lines above, so nothing here is counted twice
arithmetic.pre_generation_rule: ssh 500 + stage/launch 150 + load 450 = 1100 s, and it is ALSO rung 3's create-anchored backstop. The three spans are priced separately, as r2 priced them

recovery_arithmetic.a_second_dead_pod: STOP. After a second dead pod nothing fits and the session closes with no verdict — a THIRD pod under this registration is refused by the arithmetic and by this record. `--pre-create-check` READS `re_creations_allowed` and refuses the create itself, because at two CHEAP deaths the seconds would still fit and only the count says no

deletion_tail.rule: the span between rung 2 firing and `pod delete` stopping the meter, per pod of r1. The WORSE of the two is charged

recovery_arithmetic.rule: the recovery clause must stay REACHABLE after one dead pod. One dead pod at rung 2 plus the full worst case is 6416.54 s ≤ 6500 and $1.4259 ≤ $1.50, so ONE re-creation fits by the registered arithmetic. `--pre-create-check` computes both bounds before every create and the stricter binds
recovery_arithmetic.the_knife_edge: the widest dead pod that still leaves the whole worst case inside the stop is 583.46 s, which is WIDER than rung 2's 500 s ceiling — so a pod killed by rung 2 can never be the one that closes the recovery clause
recovery_arithmetic.the_tail_rule: rung 2's ceiling is a CREATE-ELAPSED, and the meter stops at `pod delete` and not when the rung fires. r1 measured the span between them twice — {'7spsy61lpjumrz': 78.5, 'juupgp6y77jvuz': 0.1} — and the worse of the two is charged here. So the clause is reachable at 6495.04 s ≤ 6500, a margin of 4.96 s and NOT the 83.46 s the ceiling alone implies. The runbook says «delete immediately» because of this number

request_width.rule: the margin's own reason, measured. The entity blocks nearly DOUBLE (0.96 → 1.80 a request) and the request they sit in grows by ~1 %, because a v2 request is mostly the five neighbour examples and the topic. The margin is therefore bought against a growth an order of magnitude smaller than itself — which is the direction that makes it safe, and is now a checked row rather than a sentence
request_width.sample: results/pass1_dev_pack.json leg v2 — the 200 rows the rate was measured on

seconds_per_call.rule: the MEASURED v2 figure 2.726 s/call over 200 rows (200 dev rows, pod 8tpx8lf05n6skc), × 1.25 — a named margin for the window's larger entity blocks, not the ×1.5 BOUND r2 charged before v2 had ever been measured. r2's own reading was that v2's prefill costs +18.9 % over the base and not the +50 % the bound assumed, so the margin is bought against the population's spread and not against the prompt
seconds_per_call.why_a_mean_and_not_the_slowest_call: the budget is a TOTAL over 1032 calls, so the mean is the term that belongs in it; the slowest single call in the sample was 4.066 s. Rung 4 re-prices the remainder on every poll at the LARGER of the measured mean and the last call, so a pod that is actually slower than this line is killed by the projection and not discovered in the bill

arithmetic.ssh_rule: rung 2's own ceiling, charged as a line of the budget — r2's spread, unmoved. probe-b saw ssh at 14.5 s on this card in this datacenter on 2026-08-18; on 2026-08-20 two pods were still `pod not ready` at 262.5 s and 231.9 s, both LOWER bounds; r2's own pod answered at ≤ 50 s on 2026-08-21, an UPPER bound inside the spread. Three readings, no measurement of the worst case — the ceiling stays where r2 put it
arithmetic.stage_launch_rule: scp of the bundle and the runners, the clone, the volume check and the detached launch — r2's line, unmoved. This contract's pack is larger than r2's two (results/pass1_window_pack.json against results/pass1_dev_pack.json), and the scp of one file is not what 150 s is spent on: probe-b bounds ssh + staging + launch TOGETHER at ≤ 89.5 s

A KILL at rung 2 or rung 3 is inside that window; a KILL deep inside the generation is NOT, and the clause is then a STOP and not a recovery. This is the registered arithmetic and not a defect: the seconds are what the platform holds, and pricing a re-creation at «only what remains» would open a run the cap closes. It is written down because a clause that reads as unconditional is a clause somebody will lean on at the one moment it does not hold ([[the_contracts_scope_is_narrower_than_the_rulings]])

recovery.two_meters_and_the_stricter_binds: `--pre-create-check` computes from the GATE's own ledger — the closed pods' billed seconds at their own price, which is timely and exact to the pod clock. `scripts/runpod_guard.py` reads the BALANCE delta and the billing walk, which is what the cap is defined against and which LAGS by up to ~32 min (Dv504). They are two meters and neither is the other: the gate's refuses a create the seconds cannot pay for, the guard's refuses one the money cannot. The runbook takes BOTH readings before a re-creation and the stricter binds — a clause that named one and computed the other would be true of neither ([[a_balance_delta_is_not_a_per_leg_cost]])
